explanation: L1/N660+ is a word-assembly (detokenisation) detector: it fires where a word or technical identifier is split across several BPE pieces, peaking on short, 1-3 character, non-initial pieces that carry the word's orthographic core - Greek accented 'i' inside opo[[i]]o, the elision apostrophe in qu[[']]en, 'ir' in adm[[ir]]ably, 'st' in fanta[[st]]ico, 'ch' in per[[ch]]e, 'er' in hab[[er]], 'ar' in overdecl[[ar]]atie, 'ed' in st[[ed]], and identifier pieces 'css' and ' ADVIS' - with the preceding stem piece contributing as much as the peak token itself. Whole word-initial tokens and words that fit in a single token are weak or silent (the two word-initial peaks, 'What the devil' and 'you meet', are unmodelled leftovers), and its value direction promotes long multi-morphemic academic words (' hierarch', ' asymmetry', ' kinematics', ' evolutionary') while suppressing long whitespace/indentation runs.
